_comment: Curated aliases: everyday words people type that foods.db has no token for,
mapped to a search phrase that resolves to the right canonical row.
WHY. The database is USDA-derived and uses technical names. The word 'coke'
appears in 0 of its 14,558 rows, so it could only ever resolve if the model
translated it to 'cola' itself — and on-device it did not: v8 matched
'tonic water', v10 matched nothing. Worse, the generic words that DO exist
rank badly: 'cola' resolves to 'Rum and cola' and 'soda' to 'Vodka and soda',
because cocktail rows have shorter names and the resolver's last tiebreak is
name length. Grams were right and the macros came back alcoholic.
Longest alias wins, so 'diet coke' beats 'coke'. Each target is validated
against the shipped DB by tools/db/build-aliases.mjs, which fails the build
if a phrase stops resolving to the intended row.
Keep this SMALL and high-frequency. It is a last-resort override for words
the DB genuinely cannot express, not a general synonym dictionary.

aliases.diet coke: beverages carbonated low calorie cola or pepper types with sodium saccharin contains caffeine
aliases.diet cola: beverages carbonated low calorie cola or pepper types with sodium saccharin contains caffeine
aliases.diet soda: beverages carbonated low calorie cola or pepper types with sodium saccharin contains caffeine
aliases.diet pepsi: beverages carbonated low calorie cola or pepper types with sodium saccharin contains caffeine

expect.diet coke: Beverages, carbonated, low calorie, cola or pepper-types, with sodium saccharin, contains caffeine
